tagline: Create a game. Play it. Put it on the table.

examples.prompt: Make a two-player garden drafting game we can play without knowing game design. Let us pass private hands, reward flower-and-water pairs, revise the scoring and print the full deck. Keep approved artwork when we change the rules.
examples.caption: Pocket Conservatory · original drafting rules, editable cards and printable kit

examples.prompt: Invent a solo routing puzzle with nine rotating tiles. Let me solve it by clicking the tiles, make a harder edition with fewer moves, and give me correctly sized board and tile sheets to play on paper.
examples.caption: Signal Garden · human-playable spatial puzzle and physical tiles

examples.prompt: Design a small push-your-luck game about night ferries. Let us choose to draw cargo or dock, lose only unbanked cargo in a storm, and compare repeated playtests. Then revise the valuable cargo while preserving the approved tea card.
examples.caption: Night Ferry · original risk/reward rules with editable source
